items.stem: If ΔPQR ~ ΔABC; PQ = 6 cm, AB = 8 cm and the perimeter of ΔABC is 36 cm, then the perimeter of ΔPQR is
items.answer: Similar triangles have their perimeters in the same ratio as their corresponding sides, and PQ corresponds to AB. So perimeter(ΔABC)/perimeter(ΔPQR) = AB/PQ = 8/6. Writing x for the perimeter of ΔPQR, 36/x = 8/6, so x = 36 × 6 ÷ 8 = 27. The perimeter of ΔPQR is 27 cm.

items.stem: Which of the following statement is false?
items.answer: An isosceles triangle only has two equal sides; its angles are not fixed, so two isosceles triangles need not have the same shape and need not be similar. All circles, by contrast, have the same shape and are always similar. So statement (a) is the false one.

items.stem: Two poles of height 6 m and 11 m stand vertically upright on a plane ground. If the distance between their foot is 12 m, then distance between their tops is
items.answer: Let AB = 6 m and CD = 11 m be the poles with AC = 12 m between their feet. Draw BE parallel to the ground, so BE = 12 m and DE = CD − CE = 11 − 6 = 5 m. In right triangle BED, BD² = BE² + DE² = 12² + 5² = 169, so BD = 13 m. The tops are 13 m apart.

items.stem: In a right angled ΔABC right angled at B, if P and Q are points on the sides AB and BC respectively, then
items.answer: ΔABQ and ΔCPB are right angled at B, so AQ² = AB² + BQ² and CP² = CB² + BP². Adding, CP² + AQ² = CB² + BP² + AB² + BQ² = (CB² + AB²) + (BP² + BQ²). ΔABC and ΔPBQ are also right angled at B, so those two brackets are AC² and PQ². Hence AQ² + CP² = AC² + PQ².

items.stem: It is given that, ΔABC ~ ΔEDF such that AB = 5 cm, AC = 7 cm, DF = 15 cm and DE = 12 cm then the sum of the remaining sides of the triangles is
items.answer: ΔABC ~ ΔEDF gives AB/ED = AC/EF = BC/DF, that is 5/12 = 7/EF = BC/15. From 5/12 = 7/EF, EF = 7 × 12 ÷ 5 = 16.8 cm. From 5/12 = BC/15, BC = 5 × 15 ÷ 12 = 6.25 cm. The remaining sides are EF and BC, and their sum is 16.8 + 6.25 = 23.05 cm.

items.stem: The area of a right angled triangle is 40 sq cm and its perimeter is 40 cm. The length of its hypotenuse is
items.answer: Let c be the hypotenuse and a, b the other two sides. Then a + b + c = 40 and ½ab = 40, so ab = 80 and c = 40 − (a + b). Squaring, c² = 1600 − 80(a + b) + (a + b)². Since c² = a² + b², this becomes a² + b² = 1600 − 80(a + b) + a² + 2ab + b², so 0 = 1600 − 80(a + b) + 160. Dividing by 80 gives a + b = 22, and c = 40 − 22 = 18 cm.

items.answer: AB² + BC² = 24² + 10² = 576 + 100 = 676, and AC² = 26² = 676. Since AB² + BC² = AC², the converse of Pythagoras theorem makes ΔABC right angled, so the assertion is true. items.stem: In ΔABC, AD ⊥ BC, such that AD² = BD × CD. Prove that ΔABC is right angled at A.
items.answer: From AD² = BD × CD we get AD/CD = BD/AD, and the included angles ∠ADC and ∠ADB are each 90°. By the SAS similarity criterion ΔADC ~ ΔBDA, so ∠BAD = ∠ACD and ∠DAC = ∠DBA. In ΔABC the four angles satisfy ∠BAD + ∠ACD + ∠DAC + ∠DBA = 180°, which becomes 2∠BAD + 2∠DAC = 180°, so ∠BAD + ∠DAC = 90°. That sum is ∠A, hence ∠A = 90° and ΔABC is right angled at A.

items.stem: In an equilateral triangle of side 24 cm, find the length of the altitude.
items.answer: Let ΔABC be equilateral with side 24 cm and let AD be the altitude from A, which in an equilateral triangle also bisects BC. Then BD = BC/2 = 24/2 = 12 cm and AB = 24 cm. In right ΔABD, AD = √(AB² − BD²) = √(24² − 12²) = √(576 − 144) = √432 = 12√3. Hence the altitude is 12√3 cm.

items.stem: ABC is a right triangle right angled at C. Let BC = a, CA = b, AB = c and p be the length of perpendicular from C to AB. Prove that cp = ab.
items.answer: Let CD be the perpendicular from C to AB, so CD = p and CD ⊥ AB. Taking AB as the base, the area of ΔABC is ½ × AB × CD = ½cp. Taking the legs of the right angle instead, the area of ΔABC is ½ × BC × AC = ½ab. The two expressions describe the same area, so ½cp = ½ab. Hence cp = ab.

items.stem: Two right triangles ABC and DBC are drawn on the same hypotenuse BC and on the same side of BC. If AC and BD intersect at P, prove that AP × PC = BP × DP.

In Δ BAP and Δ CDP, ∠BAP = ∠CDP = 90°, and ∠BPA = ∠CPD because they are vertically opposite angles. By the AA similarity criterion Δ BAP ~ Δ CDP. Corresponding sides are therefore proportional: BP/PC = AP/PD. Cross multiplying gives AP × PC = BP × DP. Hence proved.

items.stem: If in Δ ABC, AD is median and AE ⊥ BC, then prove that AB² + AC² = 2AD² + ½ BC².
items.answer: Draw Δ ABC with the median AD to BC and the altitude AE ⊥ BC, E lying between B and D. In right triangle ABE, Pythagoras gives AB² = AE² + BE² = (AD² − DE²) + (BD − DE)² = AD² − DE² + BD² + DE² − 2BD × DE = AD² + BD² − 2BD × DE …(1). In right triangle AEC, AC² = AE² + EC² = (AD² − ED²) + (ED + DC)² = AD² − ED² + ED² + DC² + 2ED × DC = AD² + DC² + 2DC × DE …(2). Adding (1) and (2), and using BD = DC because AD is a median, AB² + AC² = 2(AD² + BD²) = 2AD² + 2(½ BC)² = 2AD² + ½ BC². Hence proved.

In Δ APQ and Δ ABC the two pairs of sides about the common angle A are in the same ratio, AP/AB = AQ/AC, and ∠A is common, so by the SAS similarity criterion Δ APQ ~ Δ ABC. Corresponding sides are therefore proportional: AP/AB = PQ/BC, i.e. 1/3 = 4.5/BC. Hence BC = 13.5 cm.

items.stem:
In given figure Δ ABC ~ Δ DEF. AP bisects ∠CAB and DQ bisects ∠FDE.
Prove that :
(1) AP/DQ = AB/DE
(2) Δ CAP ~ Δ FDQ.
items.answer:
(1) Since Δ ABC ~ Δ DEF, corresponding angles are equal, so ∠A = ∠D. AP and DQ bisect these angles, so twice the half angle at A equals twice the half angle at D and therefore ∠BAP = ∠EDQ. Also ∠B = ∠E, again as corresponding angles. By the AA similarity criterion Δ ABP ~ Δ DEQ, so their corresponding sides give AP/DQ = AB/DE. Hence proved.
(2) Since Δ ABC ~ Δ DEF, ∠C = ∠F, and ∠A = ∠D gives, on halving, ∠CAP = ∠FDQ. With these two pairs of equal angles, the AA similarity criterion gives Δ CAP ~ Δ FDQ. Hence proved.

Comparing the two, ∠BAC = ∠DBE. Now in Δ ABC and Δ BDE we have ∠BAC = ∠DBE and ∠ACB = ∠DEB = 90°, so by the AA similarity criterion Δ ABC ~ Δ BDE. Corresponding sides give AC/BE = BC/DE, that is BE/DE = AC/BC. Hence proved.

items.stem: In the given figure, two triangles ABC and DBC lie on the same side of BC such that PQ ∥ BA and PR ∥ BD. Prove that QR ∥ AD.

Comparing (1) and (2), AQ/QC = DR/RC. In Δ ACD the points Q and R divide the sides CA and CD in the same ratio, so by the converse of the Basic Proportionality Theorem QR ∥ AD. Hence proved.

items.stem: In the given figure, BC ∥ PQ and BC = 8 cm, PQ = 4 cm, BA = 6.5 cm, AP = 2.8 cm. Find CA and AQ.

The alternate angles made by the transversal BQ give ∠CBA = ∠AQP, and ∠BAC = ∠PAQ are vertically opposite. By the AA similarity criterion Δ ABC ~ Δ AQP, so AB/AQ = BC/QP = AC/AP. Since BC/QP = 8/4 = 2, we get 6.5/AQ = 2, so AQ = 6.5/2 = 3.25 cm, and AC/2.8 = 2, so AC = 2 × 2.8 = 5.6 cm. Hence CA = 5.6 cm and AQ = 3.25 cm.

items.stem: A 6 m high tree cast a 4 m long shadow. At the same time, a flag pole cast a shadow 50 m long. How long is the flag pole?
items.answer: Let AB be the height of the tree and BC its shadow, so AB = 6 m and BC = 4 m. Let PQ be the height of the flag pole and QR its shadow, so QR = 50 m. Both shadows are cast at the same time, so the sun's angle of elevation is the same for the tree and for the pole, and both objects stand vertically on level ground. The two right triangles therefore have two pairs of equal angles, giving Δ ABC ~ Δ PQR. Corresponding sides are proportional: AB/BC = PQ/QR, that is 6/4 = PQ/50. Hence PQ = (50 × 6)/4 = 75 m. The flag pole is 75 m high.

items.stem: In the given figure, AB is a diameter of the circle with centre O. AQ, BP and PQ are tangents to the circle. Prove that ∠POQ = 90°.
items.answer:
Let the tangent PQ touch the circle at M. AQ and QM are tangents drawn to the circle from the common external point Q, so AQ = QM. In ΔOAQ and ΔOMQ we then have AQ = QM, OQ = OQ (common) and OA = OM (radii), so by the SSS congruence criterion ΔOAQ ≅ ΔOMQ, and by CPCT ∠AOQ = ∠MOQ. ...(1)
Exactly the same argument on the other side (BP and PM are tangents from P) gives ∠BOP = ∠MOP. ...(2)
AB is a diameter, so AOB is a straight line and the four angles at O add to a straight angle:
∠AOQ + ∠MOQ + ∠BOP + ∠MOP = 180°.
Substituting (1) and (2), ∠MOQ + ∠MOQ + ∠MOP + ∠MOP = 180°, so 2∠MOP + 2∠MOQ = 180°, hence ∠MOP + ∠MOQ = 90°.
Since ∠POQ = ∠MOP + ∠MOQ, we get ∠POQ = 90°. Hence proved.

items.stem: A circle with centre O and radius 8 cm is inscribed in a quadrilateral ABCD in which P, Q, R, S are the points of contact as shown. If AD is perpendicular to DC, BC = 30 cm and BS = 24 cm, then find the length DC.
items.answer:
Tangents drawn to a circle from an external point are equal in length.
From B: BR = BS = 24 cm. ...(1)
Now BC = 30 cm, and BC = BR + CR, so 24 + CR = 30, giving CR = 6 cm. ...(2)
From C: CQ = CR = 6 cm. ...(3)
In quadrilateral POQD, OP ⊥ AD and OQ ⊥ DC (a radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact), and ∠PDQ = 90° because AD ⊥ DC. By the angle sum property, ∠OPD + ∠PDQ + ∠DQO + ∠POQ = 360°, i.e. 90° + 90° + 90° + ∠POQ = 360°, so ∠POQ = 90°.
So POQD is a rectangle with two adjacent sides equal (OP = OQ = radius), i.e. a square. Hence DQ = OQ = 8 cm. ...(4)
From (3) and (4), DC = DQ + CQ = 8 + 6 = 14 cm.

items.stem: If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, then prove that the other two sides are divided in the same ratio.
items.answer:
This is the Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales theorem).
Given: a triangle ABC in which a line DE parallel to BC meets AB at D and AC at E.
To prove: AD/DB = AE/EC.
Construction: join BE and CD. Draw EN ⊥ AB and DM ⊥ AC.
Proof: ar(ADE) = ½ × AD × EN and ar(BDE) = ½ × DB × EN, so
ar(ADE)/ar(BDE) = AD/DB. ...(1)
Also ar(ADE) = ½ × AE × DM and ar(DEC) = ½ × EC × DM, so
ar(ADE)/ar(DEC) = AE/EC. ...(2)
Triangles BDE and DEC stand on the same base DE and lie between the same parallels DE and BC, so ar(BDE) = ar(DEC). ...(3)
From (1), (2) and (3), AD/DB = AE/EC.
Hence the other two sides are divided in the same ratio. Hence proved.

items.stem: In the given figure PA, QB and RC are each perpendicular to AC. If AP = x, BQ = y and CR = z, then prove that 1/x + 1/z = 1/y.
items.answer:
Here PA ⊥ AC, QB ⊥ AC and CR ⊥ AC, with AP = x, BQ = y and CR = z.
In ΔPAC and ΔQBC: ∠PAC = ∠QBC = 90° and ∠PCA = ∠QCB (common). By the AA similarity criterion ΔPAC ~ ΔQBC, so
BQ/AP = BC/AC, i.e. y/x = BC/AC. ...(1)
Similarly, in ΔACR and ΔABQ: ∠ACR = ∠ABQ = 90° and ∠CAR = ∠BAQ (common). By AA similarity ΔACR ~ ΔABQ, so
BQ/CR = AB/AC, i.e. y/z = AB/AC. ...(2)
Adding (1) and (2):
y/x + y/z = BC/AC + AB/AC = (BC + AB)/AC = AC/AC = 1,
so y(1/x + 1/z) = 1, and therefore
1/x + 1/z = 1/y. Hence proved.

items.stem: In Figure, if ΔABC ~ ΔDEF and their sides of lengths (in cm) are marked along them, then find the lengths of sides of each triangle.

From the figure, AB = 2x − 1, BC = 2x + 2, AC = 3x, DE = 18, EF = 3x + 9 and DF = 6x.
Since ΔABC ~ ΔDEF, corresponding sides are proportional:
AB/BC = DE/EF
(2x − 1)/(2x + 2) = 18/(3x + 9)
(2x − 1)(3x + 9) = 18(2x + 2)
(2x − 1)(x + 3) = 6(2x + 2)
2x² + 5x − 3 = 12x + 12
2x² − 7x − 15 = 0
2x² − 10x + 3x − 15 = 0
2x(x − 5) + 3(x − 5) = 0
(x − 5)(2x + 3) = 0, so x = 5 or x = −3/2.
A length cannot be negative, so x = 5.
In ΔABC: AB = 2(5) − 1 = 9 cm, BC = 2(5) + 2 = 12 cm, AC = 3(5) = 15 cm.
In ΔDEF: DE = 18 cm, EF = 3(5) + 9 = 24 cm, DF = 6(5) = 30 cm.

items.stem:
In ΔABC, AD is a median and O is any point on AD. BO and CO on producing meet AC and AB at E and F respectively. Now AD is produced to X such that OD = DX as shown in figure.
Prove that :
(1) EF ∥ BC
(2) AO : AX = AF : AB
items.answer:
D is the mid-point of BC (AD is a median) and OD = DX, so the segments BC and OX bisect each other at D. A quadrilateral whose diagonals bisect each other is a parallelogram, so BXCO is a parallelogram. Hence BO ∥ XC (that is, BE ∥ XC) and CO ∥ BX (that is, CF ∥ BX).
(1) In ΔABX, CF ∥ BX cuts AB at F and AX at O, so by the Basic Proportionality Theorem
AF/FB = AO/OX. ...(1)
In ΔAXC, BE ∥ XC cuts AC at E and AX at O, so by the Basic Proportionality Theorem
AE/EC = AO/OX. ...(2)
From (1) and (2), AF/FB = AE/EC, and by the converse of the Basic Proportionality Theorem, EF ∥ BC.
(2) Taking reciprocals in (1), OX/OA = FB/AF. Adding 1 to both sides,
(OX + OA)/OA = (FB + AF)/AF, i.e. AX/OA = AB/AF.
Inverting, AO/AX = AF/AB, that is AO : AX = AF : AB. Hence proved.

items.stem: In the figure, ∠BED = ∠BDE and E is the mid-point of BC. Prove that AF/CF = AD/BE.

Construction: through C draw CG ∥ FD meeting AB at G.
In ΔBDE, ∠BED = ∠BDE, so the sides opposite them are equal: BD = BE.
E is the mid-point of BC, so BE = EC.
Hence BD = BE = EC. ...(1)
In ΔBCG, DE ∥ GC, so by the Basic Proportionality Theorem
BD/DG = BE/EC = 1 (using (1)),
so DG = BD = BE = EC. ...(2)
In ΔADF, CG ∥ FD, so by the Basic Proportionality Theorem
AG/GD = AC/CF.
Adding 1 to both sides,
(AG + GD)/GD = (AC + CF)/CF, i.e. AD/GD = AF/CF.
Using GD = BE from (2),
AF/CF = AD/BE. Hence proved.

AD is the median of ΔABC, so D is the mid-point of BC and BC = 2BD.

We are given AB/PQ = AD/PM = BC/QR, so

In ΔABD and ΔPQM the three pairs of sides are therefore proportional:

Now in ΔABC and ΔPQR:

By the SAS similarity criterion, ΔABC ~ ΔPQR. Hence proved.

items.stem: In the right triangle, B is a point on AC such that AB + AD = BC + CD. If AB = x, BC = h and CD = d, then find x (in term of h and d).
items.answer:
From the figure, ΔACD is right angled at C, with B a point on AC, AB = x, BC = h and CD = d. Hence AC = AB + BC = x + h.
We are given AB + AD = BC + CD, so
AD = BC + CD − AB = h + d − x.
Applying the Pythagoras theorem in right ΔACD,
AD² = AC² + DC²
(h + d − x)² = (x + h)² + d²
(h + d − x)² − (x + h)² = d²
(h + d − x − x − h)(h + d − x + x + h) = d²
(d − 2x)(2h + d) = d²
2hd + d² − 4hx − 2xd = d²
2hd = 4hx + 2xd = 2(2h + d)x
Therefore x = hd/(2h + d).

Prove that in a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to sum of squares of other two sides.
or
Prove that in a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to sum of squares of other two sides. Using the above result, prove that, in rhombus ABCD, 4AB² = AC² + BD².
items.answer:
(1) Let ΔABC be right angled at B, so AC is the hypotenuse. Draw BE ⊥ AC.
In ΔAEB and ΔABC, ∠A is common and ∠AEB = ∠ABC (each 90°), so by AA similarity ΔAEB ~ ΔABC. Hence
AE/AB = AB/AC, giving AB² = AE × AC. ...(1)
In ΔCEB and ΔCBA, ∠C is common and ∠CEB = ∠CBA (each 90°), so by AA similarity ΔCEB ~ ΔCBA. Hence
CE/BC = BC/AC, giving BC² = CE × AC. ...(2)
Adding (1) and (2),
AB² + BC² = AE × AC + CE × AC = AC(AE + CE) = AC × AC = AC².
Thus AB² + BC² = AC². Hence proved.
(2) Let ABCD be a rhombus with diagonals AC and BD meeting at O. The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles, so
AO = OC = ½AC, BO = OD = ½BD and ∠AOB = 90°.
Applying the result just proved in right ΔAOB,
AB² = OA² + OB² = (AC/2)² + (BD/2)² = AC²/4 + BD²/4.
Multiplying throughout by 4,
4AB² = AC² + BD². Hence proved.

items.stem:
In a right triangle ABC, right angled at C. P and Q are points of the sides CA and CB respectively, which divide these sides in the ratio 2 : 1.
Prove that :  9AQ² = 9AC² + 4BC²
9BP² = 9BC² + 4AC²
9(AQ² + BP²) = 13AB²
items.answer:
P divides CA in the ratio 2 : 1, so CP = (2/3)AC; Q divides CB in the ratio 2 : 1, so QC = (2/3)BC.
ΔACQ is right angled at C, so by the Pythagoras theorem
AQ² = QC² + AC² = (2BC/3)² + AC² = (4/9)BC² + AC².
Multiplying by 9, 9AQ² = 4BC² + 9AC², i.e. 9AQ² = 9AC² + 4BC². ...(1)
ΔBCP is right angled at C, so in the same way
BP² = CP² + BC² = (2AC/3)² + BC² = (4/9)AC² + BC²,
and multiplying by 9, 9BP² = 4AC² + 9BC², i.e. 9BP² = 9BC² + 4AC². ...(2)
Adding (1) and (2),
9(AQ² + BP²) = 13AC² + 13BC² = 13(AC² + BC²).
ΔABC is right angled at C, so AC² + BC² = AB². Therefore
9(AQ² + BP²) = 13AB². Hence proved.

items.stem: Sides AB and AC and median AD of a triangle ABC are respectively proportional to sides PQ and PR and median PM of another triangle PQR. Show that ΔABC ~ ΔPQR.
items.answer:
We are given AB/PQ = AD/PM = AC/PR, where AD and PM are medians.
Construction: produce AD to E so that AD = DE, and produce PM to N so that PM = MN. Join CE and RN.
In ΔABD and ΔEDC: AD = DE (construction), ∠ADB = ∠EDC (vertically opposite) and BD = DC (AD is a median). By SAS congruence ΔABD ≅ ΔEDC, so by CPCT AB = CE. In the same way PQ = RN.
Now AE = 2AD and PN = 2PM, so from the given proportion
CE/RN = AB/PQ = 2AD/2PM = AE/PN = AC/PR.
The three pairs of sides of ΔAEC and ΔPNR are therefore proportional, so by the SSS similarity criterion ΔAEC ~ ΔPNR.
Hence the corresponding angles are equal: ∠3 = ∠4, and from the congruent triangles ∠1 = ∠2. Adding, ∠1 + ∠3 = ∠2 + ∠4, that is ∠BAC = ∠QPR.
Finally, in ΔABC and ΔPQR we have AB/PQ = AC/PR with the included angles ∠A = ∠P equal, so by the SAS similarity criterion
ΔABC ~ ΔPQR. Hence proved.

items.stem: Find the length of the second diagonal of a rhombus, whose side is 5 cm and one of the diagonals is 6 cm.
items.answer:
Let ABCD be the rhombus with AB = BC = CD = AD = 5 cm and diagonal AC = 6 cm, the diagonals meeting at O.
The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other, so
AO = OC = ½ × 6 = 3 cm,
and they bisect each other at right angles, so ΔAOB is right angled at O.
By the Pythagoras theorem in ΔAOB,
OB² = AB² − AO² = 5² − 3² = 25 − 9 = 16, so OB = 4 cm.
Since DO = OB, the second diagonal is
BD = 2 × OB = 2 × 4 = 8 cm.

items.stem: In given figure ∠1 = ∠2 and ΔNSQ ≅ ΔMTR, then prove that ΔPTS ~ ΔPRQ.
items.answer:
Since ΔNSQ ≅ ΔMTR, by CPCT ∠SQN = ∠TRM, that is ∠PQR = ∠PRQ.
Apply the angle sum property to ΔPST and to ΔPQR, both of which contain the angle at P:
∠P + ∠1 + ∠2 = ∠P + ∠PQR + ∠PRQ (each side is 180°),
so ∠1 + ∠2 = ∠PQR + ∠PRQ.
We are given ∠1 = ∠2, and we have just shown ∠PQR = ∠PRQ, so
2∠1 = 2∠PQR, giving ∠1 = ∠PQR.
Now in ΔPTS and ΔPRQ:
∠PST = ∠1 = ∠PQR,
∠QPR is common to both triangles,
and therefore the third pair of angles is equal as well.
By the AAA similarity criterion, ΔPTS ~ ΔPRQ. Hence proved.

items.stem:
Two poles, 30 feet and 50 feet tall, are 40 feet apart and perpendicular to the ground. The poles are supported by wires attached from the top of each pole to the bottom of the other, as in the figure. A coupling is placed at C where the two wires cross.
(i) What is the horizontal distance from C to the taller pole?
(ii) How high above the ground is the coupling?
(iii) How far down the wire from the smaller pole is the coupling?
items.answer:
The two poles are parallel line segments and the wires are transversals cutting through their ends, so the triangles formed are similar. Let A and B be the top and the foot of the 30 ft pole, D and E the top and the foot of the 50 ft pole, F the foot of the perpendicular from C to the ground, CF = a and FE = x, the horizontal distance from C to the taller pole.
(i) ∠CFE is a right angle. By AA similarity ΔAEB ~ ΔCEF, so
x/40 = a/30, giving 30x = 40a, i.e. a = (30/40)x.
Also by AA similarity ΔCBF ~ ΔDBE, so
a/50 = (40 − x)/40, giving 40a = 50(40 − x).
Substituting the value of a,
40 × (30/40)x = 2000 − 50x
30x = 2000 − 50x
80x = 2000, so x = 25.
The horizontal distance from C to the taller pole is 25 feet.
(ii) From x/a = 40/30 we get 30x = 40a, so 30(25) = 40a, i.e. 750 = 40a and a = 18.75.
The coupling is 18.75 feet above the ground.
(iii) The wire from the top of the smaller pole runs to the foot of the taller pole; let y be its length. By the Pythagoras theorem, 30² + 40² = y², so y = 50 feet.
Let z be the length of that wire from its top down to the coupling. The wire is cut in the same ratio as the ground beneath it, so
z/(50 − z) = (40 − 25)/25 = 15/25
25z = 15(50 − z)
5z = 3(50 − z) = 150 − 3z
8z = 150, so z = 150/8 = 18.75.
The coupling is 18.75 feet down the wire from the top of the smaller pole.

items.stem: Aakesh wanted to determine the height of a tree on the corner of his block. He knew that a certain fence by the tree was 4 feet tall. At 3 PM, he measured the shadow of the fence to be 2.5 feet tall. Then he measured the tree's shadow to be 11.3 feet. What is the height of the tree?
items.answer:
At the same moment the rays of the sun make the same angle with the ground, so the fence with its shadow and the tree with its shadow form two similar right triangles. Let x be the height of the tree.
Since the triangles are similar, the corresponding sides are proportional:
(height of the tree)/(height of the fence) = (tree shadow length)/(fence shadow length)
x/4 = 11.3/2.5
x × 2.5 = 4 × 11.3
2.5x = 45.2
x = 18.08.
The height of the tree is 18.08 feet.

items.stem: Helicopter Patrolling : A helicopter is hovering over a crowd of people watching a police standoff in a parking garage across the street. Stewart notices the shadow of the helicopter is lagging approximately 57 m behind a point directly below the helicopter. If he is 160 cm tall and casts a shadow of 38 cm at this time, what is the altitude of the helicopter?
items.answer:
The rays of the sun reach Stewart and the helicopter at the same angle, so the two right triangles formed - Stewart with his shadow, and the helicopter with its shadow - are similar. Let y be the altitude of the helicopter.
Working in metres, Stewart is 1.6 m tall and his shadow is 0.38 m long.
(height of the helicopter)/(height of Stewart) = (shadow of the helicopter)/(shadow of Stewart)
y/1.6 = 57/0.38
y = (57 × 1.6)/0.38 = (57 × 160)/38 = (3 × 160)/2 = 240.
The altitude of the helicopter is 240 m.

items.stem: The boxes used to ship some washing machines are perfect cubes with edges a. Find the length of the diagonal d of one side, and the length of the interior diagonal D (through the middle of the box).
items.answer:
The diagonal of one face joins two corners of a square of side a, so it is the hypotenuse of a 45°-45°-90° triangle with both legs equal to a.
d² = a² + a² = 2a² ⇒ d = √2 a
The interior diagonal D joins opposite corners of the cube. It is the hypotenuse of a right triangle whose legs are one edge a and one face diagonal d = √2 a.
D² = a² + d² = a² + 2a² = 3a² ⇒ D = √3 a
So the face diagonal is √2 a and the interior diagonal is √3 a.

items.stem:
Windmill : A windmill is a device for tapping the energy of the wind by means of sails mounted on a rotating shaft. Windmills still used today, mainly in parts of the world which have traditionally relied on them, are powered by electricity or water.
Anil is constructing a 8 m tall windmill supported by two wires. One wire must be 10 m long and the distance between the wires must be 21 m. Anil wanted to know what length to cut for the other wire.
items.answer:
Let the windmill stand at the point where the 8 m mast meets the ground, let x be the ground distance to the foot of the 10 m wire and y the length of the second wire, whose foot is 21 − x from the mast.
For the first wire: x² + 8² = 10², so x² = 100 − 64 = 36 and x = 6 m.
For the second wire: y² = (21 − x)² + 8² = (21 − 6)² + 8² = 15² + 8² = 225 + 64 = 289 = 17².
So y = 17 m; Anil should cut 17 m of wire for the other wire.

items.stem: Wall Paint : A painter sets a ladder up to reach the bottom of a second-story window 16 feet above the ground. The base of the ladder is 12 feet from the house. While the painter mixes the paint, a neighbour's dog bumps the ladder, which moves the base 2 feet farther away from the house. How far up the side of the house does the ladder reach?
items.answer:
First find the length l of the ladder from its original position, in which it reaches 16 feet up a wall with its foot 12 feet out.
12² + 16² = l² ⇒ 144 + 256 = 400 = l² ⇒ l = 20 feet.
After the dog bumps it the foot is 12 + 2 = 14 feet from the house, and the ladder is still 20 feet long. If h is the new height reached,
14² + h² = 20² ⇒ h = √(400 − 196) = √204 = 2√51 ≈ 14.3.
The ladder now reaches about 14.3 feet up the side of the house.

items.stem: Swimmer in Distress : A lifeguard located 20 metre from the water spots a swimmer in distress. The swimmer is 30 metre from shore and 100 metre east of the lifeguard. Suppose the lifeguard runs and then swims to the swimmer in a direct line, as shown in the figure. How far east from his original position will he enter the water? (Hint: Find the value of x in the sketch.)
items.answer:
Redraw the sketch as two triangles meeting at the point C where the lifeguard enters the water: ABC, with the lifeguard's tower AB 20 m back from the shore and the stretch x = BC along the shore, and CDE, with the remaining CD = 100 − x along the shore and the swimmer DE = 30 m out.
AB and DE are both perpendicular to the shore, so ∠ABC = ∠CDE = 90°, and the angles at C are vertically opposite and so equal. By AA similarity the two triangles are similar, hence
BC/CD = AB/DE
x/(100 − x) = 20/30 = 2/3
3x = 2(100 − x) = 200 − 2x
5x = 200 ⇒ x = 40.
The lifeguard enters the water 40 m east of his original position.

items.stem: Two Ships : Two ships are cruising together on the open ocean at 6 nautical miles per hour. One of them turns to make a angle 90° with the first and increases speed, heading for port. Assuming the first ship continues traveling at 6 knots, find the speed of the other ship if they are 10 mi apart after 1 hr.
items.answer:
After one hour the first ship has run 6 nautical miles along its original course and the second ship has run d nautical miles along a course at right angles to it, so the two runs and the 10 mile gap between the ships form a right triangle with the gap as hypotenuse.
d = √(10² − 6²) = √(100 − 36) = √64 = 8 miles.
The second ship covers 8 nautical miles in one hour, so its speed is 8 nautical miles per hour.

items.stem:
Statue of a Pineapple : The Big Pineapple is a heritage-listed tourist attraction at Nambour Connection Road, Woombye, Sunshine Coast Region, Queensland, Australia. It was designed by Peddle Thorp and Harvey, Paul Luff, and Gary Smallcombe and Associates. It is also known as Sunshine Plantation. It was added to the Queensland Heritage Register on 6 March 2009.
Ishita last year visited Nambour and wanted to find the height of a statue of a pineapple. She measured the pineapple's shadow and her own shadow. Her height is 156 cm and casts a shadow of 39 cm. The length of shadow of pineapple is 4 m. What is the height of the pineapple?
items.answer:
The sun's rays reach the pineapple and Ishita at the same angle, so the two object-and-shadow right triangles are similar and their corresponding sides are in the same ratio. Let y be the height of the pineapple and work in metres: Ishita is 1.56 m tall with a 0.39 m shadow, and the pineapple's shadow is 4 m.
height of the pineapple / height of Ishita = shadow of pineapple / shadow of Ishita
y/1.56 = 4/0.39
y = 4 × 1.56 / 0.39 = 4 × 4 = 16.
The pineapple is 16 m high.

items.stem:
Rohan is very intelligent in maths. He always try to relate the concept of maths in daily life. One day he is walking away from the base of a lamp post at a speed of 1 m/s. Lamp is 4.5 m above the ground.
(i) If after 2 second, length of shadow is 1 meter, what is the height of Rohan ?
(ii) What is the minimum time after which his shadow will become larger than his original height?
(iii) What is the distance of Rohan from pole at this point ?
(iv) What will be the length of his shadow after 4 seconds?
(v) Which similarity criterion is used in solving the above problem
items.answer:
Let the lamp be AB = 4.5 m standing at B, Rohan be CD standing at D, and E be the tip of his shadow, so DE is the shadow. AB and CD are both vertical, so ΔABE ∼ ΔCDE by AA similarity and AB/CD = BE/DE = (BD + DE)/DE.
(i) After 2 s he has walked BD = 2 × 1 = 2 m and DE = 1 m, so 4.5/CD = (2 + 1)/1 = 3, giving CD = 4.5/3 = 1.5 m = 150 cm. Rohan is 1.5 m tall.
(ii) The shadow equals his height when DE = CD = 1.5 m. Then 4.5/1.5 = (BD + 1.5)/1.5, so 3 × 1.5 = BD + 1.5 and BD = 4.5 − 1.5 = 3 m. Walking at 1 m/s that takes t = 3/1 = 3 seconds, so after 3 seconds his shadow grows longer than he is tall.
(iii) At that moment BD = 3 m, so he is 3 m from the pole.
(iv) After 4 s, BD = 1 × 4 = 4 m. Then 4.5/1.5 = (4 + DE)/DE, so 3DE = 4 + DE, 2DE = 4 and DE = 2 m.
(v) The AA similarity criterion was used.

items.stem:
The law of reflection states that when a ray of light reflects off a surface, the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.
Ramesh places a mirror on level ground to determine the height of a pole (with traffic light fired on it). He stands at a certain distance so that he can see the top of the pole reflected from the mirror. Ramesh's eye level is 1.5 m above the ground. The distance of Ramesh and the pole from the mirror are 1.8 m and 6 m respectively.
(i) Which criterion of similarity is applicable to similar triangles?
(ii) What is the height of the pole?
(iii) If angle of incidence is i , find tan i .
(iv) Now Ramesh move behind such that distance between pole and Ramesh is 13 meters. He place mirror between him and pole to see the reflection of light in right position. What is the distance between mirror and Ramesh ?
(v) What is the distance between mirror and pole?
items.answer:
Let the pole be AB standing at B, the mirror lie at M on the ground, and Ramesh be CD standing at D with C his eye. Then BM = 6 m, DM = 1.8 m and CD = 1.5 m.
(i) The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, so ∠AMB = ∠CMD, and pole and person are both vertical, so ∠ABM = ∠CDM = 90°. Two pairs of equal angles give ΔAMB ∼ ΔCMD by the AA similarity criterion.
(ii) From that similarity AB/CD = BM/DM, so AB/1.5 = 6/1.8 and AB = 1.5 × 6/1.8 = 5. The pole is 5 m high.
(iii) In right triangle CDM the angle at M is the angle of reflection, equal to i, so tan i = MD/CD = 1.8/1.5 = 6/5.
(iv) Now the pole and Ramesh are 13 m apart. Let x be the distance MD from mirror to Ramesh, so BM = 13 − x. Again AB/CD = BM/DM gives 5/1.5 = (13 − x)/x, so 5x = 1.5(13 − x) = 19.5 − 1.5x, 6.5x = 19.5 and x = 3. The mirror is 3 m from Ramesh.
(v) The mirror is then 13 − 3 = 10 m from the pole.

items.stem:
Tania is very intelligent in maths. She always try to relate the concept of maths in daily life. One day she plans to cross a river and want to know how far it is to the other side. She takes measurements on her side of the river and make the drawing as shown below.
(i) Which similarity criterion is used in solving the above problem ?
(ii) Consider the following statement :
S₁ : ∠ACB = ∠DCE
S₂ : ∠BAC = ∠CDE
Which of the above statement is/are correct.
(a) S₁ and S₂ both  (b) S₁  (c) S₂  (d) None
(iii) Consider the following statement :
S₃ : AB/DE = CA/CD
S₄ : BC/CE = AB/DE
S₅ : CA/CD = DE/AB
Which of the above statements are correct ?
(a) S₃ and S₅  (b) S₄ and S₅  (c) S₃ and S₄  (d) All three
(iv) What is the distance x across the river?
(v) What is the approximate length of AD shown in the figure?
items.answer:
In the drawing AB = 60 ft, BC = 50 ft, CE = 40 ft and DE = x, the angles at B and E are right angles, and C is the point where AD crosses BE.
(i) The AA similarity criterion is used.
(ii) ∠ABC = ∠DEC = 90° and ∠ACB = ∠DCE because they are vertically opposite, so ΔABC ∼ ΔDEC and the remaining pair ∠BAC = ∠CDE is equal too. Both statements are correct, so the answer is (a).
(iii) From ΔABC ∼ ΔDEC the corresponding sides give AB/DE = BC/CE = CA/CD, so S₃ and S₄ are correct; S₅ is wrong because CA/CD equals AB/DE, not its reciprocal DE/AB. The answer is (c).
(iv) AB/DE = BC/CE gives 60/x = 50/40, so x = 60 × 40/50 = 48. The river is 48 ft across.
(v) AC = √(60² + 50²) = √6100 ≈ 78.1 ft and CD = √(40² + 48²) = √3904 ≈ 62.5 ft, so AD = AC + CD ≈ 78.1 + 62.5 = 140.6, about 140 ft.

items.stem:
Rani wants to make the curtains for her window as shown in the figure. The window is in the shape of a rectangle, whose width and height are in the ratio 2 : 3. The area of the window is 9600 square cm.
(i) What is the shape of the window that is uncovered?
(ii) What will be the ratio of two sides of each curtain (other than hypotenuse) ?
(iii) What are the dimensions of the window ?
(iv) What will be the perimeter of the window ?
(v) How much window area is covered by the curtains?
items.answer:
(i) Each curtain is drawn back to an outer bottom corner, so the glass left showing is a triangle with its apex at the middle of the top edge and its base the full width of the window: an isosceles triangle.
(ii) Let the width be 2x and the height 3x, matching the ratio 2 : 3. A single curtain covers half the width, so its horizontal side is x, while its vertical side is the full height 3x. The ratio of those two sides is x : 3x = 1 : 3.
(iii) Area = 2x × 3x = 6x² = 9600, so x² = 1600 and x = 40 cm. The window is 2x = 80 cm wide and 3x = 120 cm high.
(iv) Perimeter = 2(80 + 120) = 400 cm.
(v) Each curtain hangs as a right triangle of base 40 cm and height 120 cm, so the pair covers 2 × ½ × 40 × 120 = 4800 cm². As a fraction of the window that is 4800/9600 × 100 = 50%, so the curtains cover half the window.

items.stem:
The centroid is the centre point of the object. It is also defined as the point of intersection of all the three medians. The median is a line that joins the midpoint of a side and the opposite vertex of the triangle. The centroid of the triangle separates the median in the ratio of 2 : 1, with the larger part towards the vertex.
On the basis of above information read the question below.
If G is centroid of △ABC with height h and J is centroid of △ADE, and line DE parallel to BC cuts △ABC at a height h/4 from BC, so that HF = h/4:
(i) What is the length of AH ?
(ii) What is the distance of point A from point G ?
(iii) What is the distance of point A from point J?
(iv) What is the distance GJ ?
items.answer:
AF is the median of △ABC from A to BC and is also its height, so AF = h, and H is where AF crosses DE.
(i) HF = h/4, so AH = AF − HF = h − h/4 = 3h/4.
(ii) G is the centroid of △ABC and AF is a median from A, so the centroid cuts it in the ratio 2 : 1 measured from the vertex: AG = ⅔ AF.
(iii) Because DE ∥ BC, AH is the median of △ADE from A, and J is the centroid of △ADE, so AJ = ⅔ AH. From part (i) AH = ¾ AF, hence AJ = ⅔ × ¾ AF = ½ AF. Part (ii) gives AF = 3/2 AG, so AJ = ½ × 3/2 AG = ¾ AG.
(iv) GJ = AG − AJ = AG − ¾ AG = ¼ AG.
